orientation.origin: on centreline, at mid-length of the length overall; Z=0 at the light load waterline drawn on the lines plan
orientation.roblox_import: export GLB with +Y up conversion; in Roblox the boat's LookVector must be set to the vessel's +X

integration.davit_limit_conflict: The liner's davit limit is published as 2000 kg. These boats are weighed, not guessed: the steam cutter is 3212 kg light and 3532 kg loaded, so a 2000 kg davit cannot hoist her. Either the davits are rated to the figures in davit_rating_required_kg, or the boat carried is the rowing cutter (1017 kg light).

export_contract.units: metres in GLB and FBX; the Roblox importer multiplies by 3.571429
export_contract.parts: one file per logical part; moving parts (oars, screw, rudder) keep their own origin
export_contract.origin_of_moving_parts: the rowlock for an oar, the shaft axis for the screw, the pintle line for the rudder

boats.name: 25 ft Steam Cutter (1888 pattern)
boats.type: steam cutter / steam tender, open boat with engine & boiler canopy
boats.reference: RMG NPC9572, 'Proposed 25ft Steam Cutter', Dangerfield Lith., 18 Jan 1888, scale 1:16

davit_attachment_points.note: two single-arm davits, one pair; slings pass under the hull at the marked stations
davit_attachment_points.lifting_eyes: forged galvanised eyebolts through the keelson at x=+2.05 and x=-1.55, 24 mm shank

boarding.boarding_point: port side amidships, abreast the after thward

footprint_for_ship.note: height includes the canopy and funnel top; funnel may be lowered for stowage under a davit head

boats.name: 25 ft Clinker Rowing Cutter (10-oared)
boats.reference: RMG SLR1818 clinker cutter; RMG SLR0772 (1838, 1:24); RMG J0780 10-oared 25 ft cutter plan

dimensions.loa_note: 7.620 m is the hull (stem head to transom). The stern-hung plate rudder shipped on the transom projects 0.30 m aft, giving 7.915 m overall; the boat is stowed and hoisted with the rudder shipped, so the stowage length below is the overall figure.

davit_attachment_points.note: single pair of davits; the boat is hoisted by two slings under the hull
davit_attachment_points.lifting_eyes: galvanised eyebolts through keelson at x=+1.95 / x=-1.60 (as on SLR1818, which shows large eyes fore and aft on the keelson for hoisting to davits)

boarding.boarding_point: port side at the after thwart; boat hooks and fenders both sides

footprint_for_ship.width_note: boats are stowed with the 3.66 m oars laid inboard along the thwarts (the davit condition); with oars out in the rowlocks the boat needs beam + 4.2 m of clear water either side, so rowing is only possible after lowering

boats.name: 27 ft Double-ended Clinker Whaler (c.1890)
boats.type: pulling/sailing sea boat, lapstrake (clinker), double ended, drop keel
boats.reference: RN 27 ft whaler type (standard seaboat from the 1890s; RNZN Naval Whalers; RMG ZAZ7497 'Whaleboat, 27ft' sectional plan)

dimensions.transom: none -- pointed stem and pointed stern (double ended)
dimensions.draft_note: documented draught is 1 ft 5 in (0.432 m) with the plate up; the solved loaded draught above is within 5 mm of it

davit_attachment_points.note: single pair of davits; hoisted by two slings, as for the cutters
davit_attachment_points.lifting_eyes: galvanised eyebolts through the keelson at x=+1.85 / x=-1.85, clear of the centreboard trunk
davit_attachment_points.mast_note: masts are 5.03 m and 3.96 m; the mainmast must be lowered to hoist under davits with less than 5 m of headroom above the sheer

boarding.boarding_point: port side at the after thwart, inboard of the mizzen
boarding.oars_note: five oars single banked -- three on the port side, two on the starboard side -- as the type was pulled

footprint_for_ship.height_note: with the mainmast stepped; 0.45 m with both masts struck and laid in the boat
